Title: Small and low-intensity fires missed by satellite monitoring
Novelty_Justification: Well-studied problem with many papers on burned area mapping. UNet++ and similar approaches are recent but the problem space is crowded. Novelty is in operational deployment not methods.
Tractability_Justification: Clean satellite data (Landsat/Sentinel-2) with clear evaluation metrics (burned area vs. reference). Existing benchmarks and training data. Signal is strong for moderate-to-large burns.
Feasibility_Justification: Freely available satellite data. Compute manageable. But validation of small-fire detection requires airborne reference data or field verification that adds cost and logistics.
Confidence_Justification: High confidence that improved detection is achievable -- Potter et al. 2026 already showed F1=0.85. The question is incremental improvement toward operational deployment.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Important for carbon accounting accuracy. Small fires individually have small impact but collectively matter. Not an existential ecological question.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Classic ML + remote sensing problem. Image segmentation on satellite data is a core competency for someone with strong deep learning skills.

Title: No operational fire spread prediction for boreal forests
Novelty_Justification: ML-based fire spread prediction for boreal forests is thin. The BCWildfire benchmark appeared only in 2024. Boreal-specific physics-informed ML is largely unexplored.
Tractability_Justification: Hard problem: heterogeneous fuels and complex topography create high-dimensional prediction space. Limited training data for rare extreme events. Fire spread is partially chaotic.
Feasibility_Justification: BCWildfire dataset freely available. But operational integration requires fire agency partnerships and real-time data pipelines that go beyond academic research.
Confidence_Justification: Real risk of null result: fire spread may be too stochastic for useful prediction at operational timescales. Weather prediction errors compound into fire prediction errors.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Better prediction saves lives and improves resource allocation. The 2023 Canadian season (15-18 Mha) demonstrated the human cost of inadequate prediction.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Deep learning on spatiotemporal data is a strong match. Physics-informed ML and multimodal data fusion are good growth areas. Domain expertise needed but not binding.

Title: Short-interval reburns increasing with no operational reburn risk product
Novelty_Justification: Very few computational products exist for reburn probability mapping. The fire atlas provides infrastructure but nobody has built the integration layer. A genuine gap.
Tractability_Justification: Data exists: fire history from satellite archives and weather projections from climate models. Clear target variable (did reburn occur?). But training data for short-interval reburns is sparse because events were rare until recently.
Feasibility_Justification: Satellite fire history freely available. Fire weather projections from climate models accessible. Fuel recovery trajectories need some field calibration but literature provides starting points.
Confidence_Justification: Plausible that a reburn probability model would outperform the current baseline (which is nothing). Ecological consequences of type conversion are harder to predict but the risk mapping itself is tractable.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Reburns can trigger irreversible biome conversion -- black spruce to deciduous shrubland. This is a regime shift with century-scale carbon consequences. Over 400k ha reburned in NWT in 2023 alone.
Skill_Fit_Justification: ML classification/regression on remote sensing time series. Spatial risk modeling. Good fit for someone who can build predictive models from satellite-derived features.

Title: Spectral recovery after fire does not indicate ecological recovery
Novelty_Justification: Well-documented mismatch in individual papers but no operational product distinguishes spectral from compositional recovery. The gap between documentation and solution is the novelty.
Tractability_Justification: Distinguishing conifer from deciduous regrowth is possible with red-edge and hyperspectral data but not easy at scale. Ground truth for compositional recovery is sparse across the boreal zone.
Feasibility_Justification: Requires long time series (decades) and species-level validation data. Hyperspectral satellite missions (CHIME/SBG) not yet operational. HLS and Sentinel-2 red-edge are available now but may not suffice.
Confidence_Justification: Could likely distinguish broad categories (conifer vs. deciduous) but fine-scale compositional recovery assessment from orbit may not achieve the accuracy needed for carbon accounting.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Systematic bias in post-fire carbon accounting has real consequences for climate policy. If spectral recovery masks compositional shifts the carbon models are wrong.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Time series analysis and multi-sensor fusion are strong ML fits. Species-level classification from satellite data is a well-defined computer vision problem.

Title: Boreal carbon sink weakening but monitoring too coarse for regional attribution
Novelty_Justification: Carbon sink monitoring is heavily studied at global scale. Regional attribution using multi-source satellite fusion is less developed for the boreal specifically but conceptually familiar.
Tractability_Justification: Multiple interacting causes (fire/insects/drought/logging/permafrost) at different scales. Atmospheric inversions give continental estimates. Disentangling causes at useful spatial resolution is genuinely hard.
Feasibility_Justification: Requires integrating OCO-2 and GOSAT inversions with SIF and LiDAR biomass and fire emissions and ground flux data. Large-scale data fusion across very different data types. Multi-year effort.
Confidence_Justification: Real risk that the problem is too underdetermined. Atmospheric inversions cannot isolate sub-regional drivers with current satellite coverage. Ground data too sparse for validation.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Fundamental question for climate policy. If the boreal sink has flipped to a source (as 2023 data suggest for Canada) this changes global carbon budgets and UNFCCC commitments.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Data fusion and ML regression are applicable. But atmospheric science and carbon cycle modeling are deep specialist domains. The binding constraint is domain knowledge not computation.

Title: Permafrost thaw monitored at point scale but not landscape scale in forested regions
Novelty_Justification: InSAR permafrost monitoring in tundra is established. Forested permafrost is the hard frontier. NISAR L-band is brand new (operational Jan 2026) and its forest-permafrost products don't exist yet.
Tractability_Justification: Fundamental physics challenge: L-band InSAR has better coherence through vegetation than C-band but still noisy. Signal extraction from forested terrain requires novel processing approaches.
Feasibility_Justification: NISAR data freely available since Feb 2026 through ASF DAAC. Processing infrastructure exists. But field validation of permafrost measurements requires access to remote boreal-permafrost overlap zones.
Confidence_Justification: Uncertain whether NISAR L-band will be sufficient for permafrost monitoring under forest canopy. May need multi-year data stacking. The sensor is new and the answer is genuinely unknown.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Fire-permafrost feedback may be the most dangerous positive feedback in the boreal carbon system. Turetsky et al. 2020 estimate abrupt thaw could double the permafrost carbon feedback.
Skill_Fit_Justification: InSAR processing and time series analysis are learnable technical skills. But SAR interferometry is specialized and the permafrost interpretation requires geophysics knowledge.

Title: Boreal peatland methane emissions rising but cannot be attributed at landscape scale
Novelty_Justification: Methane monitoring from TROPOMI is active. Landscape-scale attribution in peatlands is less developed. The fusion of multiple sensor types for process attribution is somewhat novel.
Tractability_Justification: Diffuse emissions and episodic ebullition and coarse satellite resolution create a genuinely hard inverse problem. Top-down and bottom-up estimates disagree by 2-3x after years of effort.
Feasibility_Justification: Requires combining TROPOMI methane and InSAR water table and SAR wetland mapping and likely eddy covariance ground data. Multi-sensor multi-domain fusion with sparse ground truth.
Confidence_Justification: High risk that the problem remains underdetermined at landscape scale. The top-down/bottom-up disagreement has persisted despite new satellite data. Incremental progress likely but breakthrough unlikely.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Methane is 80x more potent than CO2 over 20 years. If boreal peatland methane is increasing due to warming this is a critical climate feedback. Understanding attribution enables intervention.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Atmospheric inversions and wetland biogeochemistry are deep specialist domains. The ML angle is mostly data fusion which fits but the domain expertise gap is wide. [SKILL FIT BIAS: score reflects computational profile not importance]

Title: Boreal soil carbon stocks below 30 cm are essentially unmapped
Novelty_Justification: InSAR-based peat thickness estimation is new. Most SOC models stop at 30 cm. The deep-peat mapping angle is genuinely underexplored.
Tractability_Justification: Remote sensing cannot directly measure deep soil carbon. All approaches are indirect proxies (subsidence rates and vegetation type and topography). The heterogeneity of peatland carbon at sub-100m scales is well-documented.
Feasibility_Justification: Deep soil coring for validation is expensive destructive and logistically hard in remote boreal terrain. Existing training data for deep peat is very sparse (NCSCDv2 has 25-50% uncertainty).
Confidence_Justification: Uncertain whether indirect proxies can predict deep SOC at useful accuracy. The spatial variability of peat depth and carbon density is high and may exceed what satellite proxies can resolve.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Deep SOC is the pool that matters most for permafrost carbon feedback. Underestimating it means underestimating climate risk. Also relevant for peatland restoration carbon credits.
Skill_Fit_Justification: ML regression with sparse training data and indirect features. The problem is solvable in principle but the data limitations are binding. Fieldwork capacity would matter more than ML expertise.

Title: Boreal tree cover shifting northward but treeline ecotone poorly resolved
Novelty_Justification: Treeline monitoring from space is active but the ecotone resolution problem is specific and the fusion approach (ICESat-2 height + spectral data for continuous mapping) is well-defined and less explored.
Tractability_Justification: ICESat-2 provides height samples at footprint resolution. Sentinel-2/Landsat provide spectral data. The fusion problem has clear inputs and outputs. Well-posed regression/classification.
Feasibility_Justification: Freely available satellite data. Compute manageable. But validation at the ecotone requires measurements in remote high-latitude locations. Field logistics are expensive.
Confidence_Justification: Reasonable confidence that fusing LiDAR height with spectral data can improve treeline mapping beyond current products. The continuous-gradient nature makes evaluation tricky but the approach is sound.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Treeline advance affects albedo (dark forest absorbs more than tundra) and carbon stocks. Important but the advance is slow (decades) and the albedo feedback is smaller than fire/permafrost feedbacks.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Multi-sensor data fusion + ML regression/classification at landscape scale. This is a natural fit for strong remote sensing and ML skills. The computational challenge is well-matched.

Title: Bark beetle outbreaks cannot be detected early enough from satellites
Novelty_Justification: Heavily studied problem with many papers on spectral detection. The multi-scale integration (satellite + UAV) is somewhat novel but not a new idea.
Tractability_Justification: Fundamental resolution-coverage tradeoff. Green attack phase is at the detection limit of Sentinel-2. The spectral signal only becomes reliable at moderate-to-severe defoliation which is too late.
Feasibility_Justification: Satellite data available. Drone surveys require field access and operational capacity. Multi-scale integration adds logistical complexity. Partnerships with forest management agencies needed.
Confidence_Justification: Moderate. Sentinel-2 alone likely cannot achieve reliable green-attack detection. Drone augmentation works at plot scale but doesn't scale to landscape. The tradeoff may be fundamental.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Bark beetles are expanding northward into boreal Fennoscandia. Economic losses from the 2018-2022 European outbreak exceeded 500M cubic meters of spruce. Damage is accelerating.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Computer vision and change detection and multi-scale analysis are good ML fits. Drone image processing adds a hands-on component. The resolution-coverage tradeoff is a systems design problem.

Title: Spruce budworm defoliation mapping lags behind outbreak timeline
Novelty_Justification: Well-studied with many Sentinel-2 papers. The prediction component (forecasting outbreak front movement) is less developed but not absent.
Tractability_Justification: Early defoliation hard to distinguish from phenological variation and drought stress. Spectral signal improves with severity but that's too late for early intervention.
Feasibility_Justification: Sentinel-2 data freely available. Aerial survey data for validation exists. Existing ML classifiers and spectral indices identified. Lower barrier to entry than some other problems.
Confidence_Justification: Detection improvement is likely incremental. The real breakthrough would be predicting where outbreaks spread next season which requires population dynamics modeling beyond spectral analysis.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Current outbreak in Quebec/Atlantic Canada affects millions of hectares. SBW is the most destructive insect pest in North American boreal forests. Economic and ecological costs are massive.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Spectral classification and time series analysis and ML prediction models. Strong computational fit. But entomological domain knowledge needed for population dynamics modeling.

Title: Boreal wetland classification inadequate for carbon and biodiversity assessments
Novelty_Justification: Heavily studied area with many SAR-optical fusion papers. Boreal peatland sub-type classification is more specific but still well-explored. Novelty is incremental.
Tractability_Justification: Multi-temporal SAR helps discriminate wetland types. Deep learning outperforms traditional classifiers. Clear improvement pathway. But transferability across boreal regions is poor -- models trained in one area fail elsewhere.
Feasibility_Justification: Data available but training labels for peatland sub-types are scarce and require expert field identification. Creating a pan-boreal training dataset is a multi-year effort requiring multiple field campaigns.
Confidence_Justification: Incremental improvement likely. But the spectral/SAR similarity of peatland sub-types (especially treed bog vs. treed fen) may be a fundamental limit for satellite-based classification.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Bogs and fens have fundamentally different carbon dynamics and biodiversity value. Misclassification means carbon accounting errors and mis-targeted restoration spending.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Multi-sensor fusion and deep learning classification are core ML competencies. SAR processing and time series analysis fit well.

Title: Caribou habitat loss monitored at coarse scales but not at management resolution
Novelty_Justification: Caribou habitat mapping is well-studied in conservation biology. Multi-scale computational integration is less developed but the components all exist individually.
Tractability_Justification: Requires combining landscape-level disturbance (Landsat) with stand-level structure (LiDAR) and ground-level lichen cover. Multiple scales and multiple data sources with different spatial resolutions.
Feasibility_Justification: Satellite data available but linear feature mapping at scale requires significant processing effort. Lichen ground-truthing requires field work. Connectivity modeling needs population data.
Confidence_Justification: Better habitat maps would improve management decisions but caribou population response to habitat quality involves predator-prey dynamics and other factors beyond habitat alone.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Caribou are legally threatened across Canada. Federal policy requires 65% undisturbed habitat. Getting habitat quality wrong has direct regulatory consequences. Flagship species for boreal conservation.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Remote sensing + GIS + connectivity modeling. Solid computational fit but ecological interpretation of habitat quality for caribou requires domain expertise. [SKILL FIT BIAS: ecological knowledge is binding]

Title: Russia's boreal forest monitoring is a data black hole
Novelty_Justification: Satellite-only monitoring with uncertainty quantification for a validation-free zone is genuinely novel as a computational challenge. Transfer learning across boreal regions is underexplored.
Tractability_Justification: Fundamental problem is absence of ground truth. Transfer learning from Canadian/Fennoscandian boreal is plausible but inherently unvalidatable in the target domain. You can't test what you can't access.
Feasibility_Justification: Satellite data is available globally. Processing infrastructure exists. But without Russian collaboration there is no path to field validation. Geopolitical situation shows no signs of resolving.
Confidence_Justification: Real risk that satellite-only products for Russia will have unknown and potentially large systematic errors. Without validation you cannot know whether your models transfer correctly.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Russia holds 65% of global boreal forest and ~50% of permafrost. If Siberian fire emissions are under-counted or permafrost thaw is unmonitored the global carbon budget is wrong.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Domain adaptation and uncertainty quantification are good ML problems. But the scale is enormous and the validation gap may be unfillable. The constraint is access not computation.

Title: SIF-based drought stress monitoring in boreal forests promising but unvalidated
Novelty_Justification: SIF for drought is emerging research. Boreal-specific validation is thin. The early-warning angle (detecting stress before structural damage) is novel for boreal conifers.
Tractability_Justification: TROPOMI SIF data available since 2018. Signal-drought relationship being established in other biomes. Downscaling from 7 km to ecologically meaningful scales is a well-defined computational problem.
Feasibility_Justification: Satellite data freely available. Validation possible at boreal flux tower sites (Hyytiala in Finland and SOBS in Saskatchewan). Lower logistical barrier than most field-dependent problems.
Confidence_Justification: SIF-drought relationship established elsewhere but boreal conifers have unique physiology -- sustained greenness under drought stress and winter photosynthesis shutdown. Transfer may not work cleanly.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Drought stress detection enables proactive management (bark beetle monitoring and fire readiness) but the causal chain from detection to conservation action is indirect. Not an existential ecological question.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Satellite data analysis and ML regression and sensor fusion/downscaling are core competencies. Tower-based validation is straightforward if site access is arranged.

Title: Intact forest landscapes shrinking faster than they are being protected
Novelty_Justification: IFL monitoring exists (GFW). Conservation planning tools exist (Marxan/Zonation). Applying predictive fragmentation modeling to boreal IFL protection is somewhat novel but not groundbreaking.
Tractability_Justification: Clear data inputs: road networks and concession boundaries and fire probability and connectivity metrics. Spatial optimization tools are mature and well-documented. Problem is well-posed.
Feasibility_Justification: GFW data freely available. Forestry concession data available in Canada and Fennoscandia (not Russia). Conservation planning software is open-source. Compute manageable.
Confidence_Justification: High confidence that spatial prioritization can identify high-value IFLs at risk. Less confidence that computational outputs translate to actual protection decisions. The bottleneck is political will not analysis.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: IFLs are the most ecologically intact remnants of the boreal biome. Their loss is irreversible on management timescales. Permafrost carbon under IFLs adds climate urgency.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Spatial optimization and GIS and predictive modeling. Good computational fit. But conservation planning has its own methodological traditions that need to be respected.

Title: Indigenous Guardian programs need purpose-built computational tools
Novelty_Justification: Very few examples of computational tools designed from the ground up for Indigenous monitoring frameworks rather than adapted from industry. A genuine design-research gap.
Tractability_Justification: This is as much a social and participatory design problem as a technical one. OCAP principles and data sovereignty and cultural integration are not ML problems. The technical component is the easier part.
Feasibility_Justification: Requires deep sustained engagement with Indigenous communities. Cannot be done as a solo computational project. Long timescales (years) and relationship-building are prerequisites.
Confidence_Justification: Real risk that a computationally-designed tool fails to serve community needs. Tech-for-development track record is mixed. Success depends on co-design not technical sophistication.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Guardian programs cover vast boreal territories. Better tools could amplify monitoring capacity significantly. Cultural and ecological value of supporting Indigenous-led conservation is high.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Requires participatory design and social science and community engagement skills more than ML. The computational component (GIS mapping and remote sensing delivery) is secondary. [SKILL FIT BIAS: important problem penalized by computational framing]

Title: Storm damage detection in boreal forests is slow and incomplete
Novelty_Justification: Well-studied with many SAR papers published since 2019. L-band SAR from NISAR is the obvious next step and the data is now available. Low novelty.
Tractability_Justification: Clean SAR change detection problem. Before/after pairs with well-defined target (canopy loss). Signal is strong for areal windthrow. Multi-frequency SAR (C+L band) is a straightforward extension.
Feasibility_Justification: Sentinel-1 and NISAR data freely available. SAR processing infrastructure is mature (SNAP/ASF). Commercial high-res SAR available for rapid response. Low barriers to entry.
Confidence_Justification: High confidence that NISAR L-band will improve windthrow detection sensitivity especially for partial damage. Multi-frequency fusion has clear physics justification.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Windthrow is ecologically important for wildlife habitat and fire fuel loading but not as urgent as fire/carbon/permafrost problems. Economic importance mainly in Fennoscandia for timber salvage.
Skill_Fit_Justification: SAR processing + ML change detection is a clean well-defined technical problem. Multi-frequency SAR analysis is a growth area with clear computational challenges.

Title: Bioacoustic monitoring of boreal biodiversity limited by lack of boreal-specific ML models
Novelty_Justification: Boreal-specific acoustic classifiers are genuinely underexplored. Foundation models for bioacoustics are emerging (2024-2025) but not tuned for boreal species assemblages or acoustic environments.
Tractability_Justification: The ML problem is well-defined: fine-tune acoustic classifiers on boreal recordings. Transfer learning from general-purpose models to boreal-specific acoustic environments is a tractable research question.
Feasibility_Justification: Requires field deployment of recording units in boreal forests and expert annotation of recordings. Hardware is cheap (~$200/unit) but annotation is labor-intensive and requires ornithological expertise.
Confidence_Justification: Reasonable confidence that a boreal-tuned acoustic classifier would outperform general-purpose models. BirdNET and similar tools already work moderately well -- the question is how much boreal-specific fine-tuning helps.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Continuous biodiversity monitoring would detect range shifts and population declines earlier than periodic field surveys. Climate-driven changes in boreal bird communities are occurring now.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Audio ML and transfer learning and fine-tuning foundation models are strong computational fits. The problem is well-scoped for someone with ML expertise and access to field sites.

Title: Mining footprint monitoring lacks ecological recovery tracking integration
Novelty_Justification: Mine monitoring with satellites exists and is approaching operational. Ecological recovery tracking from space is less developed but conceptually straightforward. Novelty is in the long-term integration.
Tractability_Justification: Time series analysis of NDVI and canopy height recovery with well-defined study sites (mines have clear boundaries). Recovery trajectories can be compared across sites and reclamation methods.
Feasibility_Justification: Satellite data available. Mine boundaries known. Historical imagery covers the 10-30 year timescales needed. But ground truth for ecosystem function recovery requires site access and ecological expertise.
Confidence_Justification: NDVI recovery is straightforward to track but ecosystem function recovery (species diversity and soil development and hydrology) is much harder to assess from space. Risk of measuring cosmetic recovery only.
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Localized impact compared to pan-boreal problems like fire or carbon sink. Individual mine sites matter but the aggregate footprint is small relative to logging or fire disturbance.
Skill_Fit_Justification: Time series analysis and change detection and vegetation mapping are strong computational fits. Well-defined study sites reduce logistical complexity.
